sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Franchise Licensing and Syrups Supply Chain for Bubble Tea Chains

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama maintains an active network of bilateral investment agreements and double taxation agreements, including with Spain, Netherlands, United Kingdom, Singapore, Mexico, and other jurisdictions; the United States–Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA, effective 2012) is a key Western Hemisphere instrument containing an investment chapter with substantive protections for covered investments.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 23 of 2015 on Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism, as amended (including Law No. 60 of 2017 and Law No. 70 of 2021); Executive Decree No. 363 of 2015; Resolution No. 142-13 of 2021 or successor implementing regulations of the Registro Público de Panamá establishing the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (UBO Registry); and applicable rulemaking of the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) and the Financial Intelligence Unit (UAF).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney executed by each proposed shareholder/director appointing the Panamanian resident agent or registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian notary or foreign notary if executed outside Panama
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for origin-country documents; otherwise consular legalization through a Panamanian embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Name Reservation / Vista de Nombre (Certificado de Búsqueda de Nombre)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: None required within Panama; apostille only if the certificate is to be used abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Declaration of Ultimate Beneficial Owner under Law 70 of 2021, with ownership trajectory down to ultimate natural persons
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public / law firm authorized by the Registro Público de Panamá
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if signed outside Panama and required for foreign public-file reliance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Apostilled Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent certificate for any participating corporate shareholder (if the shareholder is an existing legal entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or competent authority in the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille pursuant to the Hague Apostille Convention; otherwise consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under Law 23 of 2015 and Executive Decree 363 of 2015 requires identification of all natural person beneficial owners and directors. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) must be subjected to enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds analysis. Screening is mandatory against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU/UK sanctions lists, and the domestic financial intelligence list maintained by the Panamanian Financial Intelligence Unit. All UBO declarations must be kept current and filed with the Beneficial Owner Registry; failure to disclose triggers severe administrative penalties and potential criminal liability for money-laundering predicate offenses.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Sede Electrónica / Portal de Servicios en Línea del Registro Público (official online portal: www.registro.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be submitted in Spanish or in a language using the Latin script transliterated without diacritical marks that might create confusing similarity. The Registro Público applies strict phonetic and spelling comparison; names are evaluated for identity or confusing similarity with existing registered companies. A name may include English or other Latin-script terms, but the public registry may require a Spanish-language component if the proposed name could mislead the public as to activity or nationality.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant or the residue agent receives a formal rejection notice citing the Registry's grounds. Under the general administrative procedure law of Panama (Ley 38 de 2000), the applicant may file a written reconsideration petition (recurso de reconsideración) with the Registro Público within five business days of notification. If the rejection is confirmed, the applicant may file a hierarchical appeal before the Director General of the Registro Público, and ultimately the matter may be pursued in the Contencioso-Administrativo jurisdiction before the Supreme Court of Justice. In practice, rejection is usually corrected for typographic or phonetic similarity by filing a new name reservation request; an extension of the existing reservation is available only by a fresh filing before the expiration of the 540-day window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Allowed. A Panama S.A. may operate with a virtual office provided it maintains a registered office and resident agent at a physical Panamanian address. For franchise licensing, royalty collection, and syrup supply chains, the tax authority generally recognizes the resident agent's address as the statutory seat. However, the company must retain complete accounting and corporate records either at the registered agent's office or at another designated location within Panamanian territory if required for inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: less than 5% annual likelihood for unannounced physical inspections for a low-risk franchise licensing and supply-chain entity with a virtual office. Competent tax and AML authorities may issue remote information requests or audit letters; targeted inspections are possible if a risk flag arises, but the baseline probability is materially low.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and reservation (Vista de Nombre and Certificado de No Inscripción)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for electronic name reservation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of incorporation documents and UBO declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff and prevailing market fee scale

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille of authentication for foreign-executed powers and corporate instruments (two apostilles estimated)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama (Cancillería)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration filing of Articles of Incorporation and supplementary documentation at the Registro Público de Panamá
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff based on authorized capital structure; approximate for a standard USD 10,000 authorized capital S.A.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and registered office service – first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian resident agent (law firm or trust company)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for low-risk service corporations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Panamanian legal counsel preparation of charter, bylaws, corporate governance minutes, and UBO register filings
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional fee benchmark for a standard S.A. incorporation package

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Panama Law No. 32 of 26 February 1927 (General Stock Corporation Law - Ley General de Sociedades Anónimas), as amended by Law No. 24 of 1966 and Law No. 25 of 1971; Public Registry Regulation No. 1 of 2016, Articles 10-35 (as applicable to Sociedad Anónima incorporation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Dirección General, Sección Mercantil
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificado de No Homonimia and Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad Anónima (Public Deed of Incorporation duly notarized and inscribed in the Folio Mercantil)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Panama S.A. under Law 32 of 1927; the Articles typically authorize USD 10,000 divided into ordinary shares, which may be issued without immediate payment. No mandatory escrow account is required for a standard non-regulated corporation; escrow and paid-up evidence become relevant only if the company later engages in banking or CLIC-regulated activities.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the subscriptions to the capital stock of Sociedad Anónima, as set out in the Articles of Incorporation, be and they are hereby accepted and recorded in the corporate register; (2) that the registered office is established at the address of the appointed resident agent for purposes of service and statutory filings; (3) that the initial Officers be and hereby are appointed President, Secretary and Treasurer, with full corporate powers; (4) that the officers and counsel are authorized to open bank accounts, execute bank resolution forms, promote the franchise licensing and syrups supply business in Panama; and (5) that the issuance of the founder shares be ratified for value received.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Public Registry Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Dirección General (online via PANATRÁMITE portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written application for a Certificado de No Homonimia requesting one primary corporate name and two alternative names. The registry electronically screens for identical or confusingly similar names against the mercantile register. Upon clearance, the certificate is valid for 30 days for use in the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application signed by the applicant
Copy of the applicant's passport or cédula de identidad
Statement of corporate purpose including ISIC 5610 franchise and syrup supply activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, resubmit within 3 business days using alternative names; request priority review through the registry's customer service office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de la República de Panamá (licensed notary of the incorporator)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct Panama counsel to draft the Escritura Pública de Constitución containing the corporate name, domicile, term, share capital, board structure, and resident agent appointment. All incorporators must appear before the notary to execute the deed. The resident agent (a licensed lawyer or firm) signs the acceptance of office.
required_dossiers: Certificado de No Homonimia
Passport copies of all incorporators and original documents for notarial identification
Draft articles of incorporation and by-laws
Signed acceptance letter of the resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary may issue a marginal correction note for typographical or clerical defects before submission to the Public Registry; substantial amendments require a new deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Corporation in the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the fully notarized Escritura with the Mercantile Section accompanied by a copy of the fiscal closure receipt. Pay the registry inscription fee calculated on authorized capital. Once the Registrar issues the auto de inscripción, the S.A. acquires legal personality and the company receives its Folio Mercantil certificate and registration number.
required_dossiers: Notarized Escritura Pública de Constitución
Certificado de No Homonimia
Receipt of inscription fee payment
Duly signed resident agent acceptance
Completed registry filing form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a defect notice (prevención), respond within the statutory term, typically 10 business days, with a clarifying brief and, if needed, a notarial correction amendment; further judicial appeal lies to the First Instance Administrative Court of the Registro Público.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration (RUC) and Municipal Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipio de Panamá - Ventanilla Única de Licencias (VUL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the RUC application for the S.A. in the DGI e-Reforma system to obtain the Registro Único de Contribuyente and electronic signature certificate. Thereafter, submit the Aviso de Operación through the VUL portal with a sworn declaration describing the franchise licensing, syrup production, and wholesale supply activities, together with documentation of the physical office/warehouse address.
required_dossiers: Public Registry certificate of incorporation (Folio Mercantil)
DGI Form RUC-11 and applicant identification
Proof of lease or property title for the registered and operating premises
Sworn statement and VUL form for Aviso de Operación
Fire safety inspection certificate for the physical premises (if already obtained)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality returns the Aviso de Operación for corrections due to zoning or use classification, review the technical objection in the VUL platform, resubmit the corrected sworn statement and floor plan, and re-file within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sanitary Registration for Food-Grade Syrups and Beverage Components
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) - Dirección de Regulación de Alimentos
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For any facility producing, importing, or repackaging syrups, toppings, or boba ingredients, obtain a Registro Sanitario de Alimentos for each distinct product line and a certificate of sanitary operation for the plant. The technical file must include formulations, labels, and proof of compliance with mineral water and food additive standards.
required_dossiers: Aviso de Operación or municipal license of the facility
Product technical file, formulas, and additive declarations
Plant layout and water quality certificates
HACCP plan and traceability manual
Proposed label artwork in Spanish
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the MINSA technical observation letter within 15 business days by amending the dossier; if registration is denied, file a reconsideration appeal before the Dirección de Regulación de Alimentos within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Environmental, and Civil Defense Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI); Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE); Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de la República de Panamá (BCBRP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure the MICI industrial operation permit for syrup manufacturing or packing activities, complete the environmental entry process in MiAMBIENTE's Sistema de Información Ambiental (SIA), and obtain the BCBRP fire safety inspection certificate (Visto Bueno) covering exit routes, extinguishers, and sprinklers for any physical plant or warehouse.
required_dossiers: Aviso de Operación and RUC registration
Form SIA-1 environmental classification screening for light food manufacturing
Facility floor plan with fire safety systems
Wastewater and solid waste handling declarations
MICI industrial permit application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BCBRP issues a non-compliance certificate, correct the identified deficiencies, schedule re-inspection, and pay the re-inspection fee; for environmental objections, submit a supplementary explanation or adjust the classification request within the MiAMBIENTE review window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) - Dirección Nacional de Servicios a las Empresas y Regulación de Industria
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permiso de Operación Industrial (MICI) combined with Aviso de Operación (Municipio de Panamá) and Registro Sanitario de Alimentos (MINSA) for the syrup and tea ingredient supply lines.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II - Estudio de Impacto Ambiental (EsIA) abridged for small-to-mid scale food and beverage processing plants; light activity may qualify as Category I (Registro) if throughput is below the regulatory threshold.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with MiAMBIENTE Resolution AG-0328-2018 (BOD5 ≤ 250 mg/L, COD ≤ 500 mg/L, TSS ≤ 350 mg/L, pH 6-9) for process effluent or industrial sewer disposal; VOC and particulate emissions from syrup boiling or packing lines must meet applicable air quality standards under Executive Decree No. 5 of 2009, as amended; solid and plastic beverage-container waste must be managed under Integrated Waste Management Law No. 8 of 2017 through certified handlers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Visto Bueno) from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de la República de Panamá, including NFPA-compliant exit routes, extinguishers and alarm systems; structural load inspection for warehouse stacking of syrup containers; workplace hygiene and safety clearance by the Dirección General de Salud del Ministerio de Salud and registration of the workplace and employees with the Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) and MITRADEL occupational risk program.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Autoridad Nacional de Ingresos Públicos (ANIP) – formerly Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; official portal: https://www.anip.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must (1) engage a duly licensed Panamanian lawyer and register as a Panama branch or reproduce its incorporation or foreign company registration with the Public Registry; (2) file the public deed, bylaws or constitutive documents, and evidence of appointment of a resident agent and legal representative with the ANIP; (3) obtain a permanent/non-resident RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) through the ANIP electronic portal; (4) issue an 'Aviso de Operación' or aviso de inscripción to commence activities; (5) obtain a digital signature certificate for electronic filings; and (6) register as an ITBMS taxpayer, if applicable. The complete procedure generally takes 2–5 business days after presentation of apostilled and Spanish-translated documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a US-style check-the-box system. A Sociedad Anónima (S.A.) is an entity-level taxpayer subject to corporate income tax only on Panama-source income. Available statutory elections include the 'Pequeño Contribuyente' (small taxpayer) regime for annual gross income up to B/.150,000, optional grouping or consolidated filing for qualifying economic groups, elections regarding transferable tax-loss carryforwards, and the CFC/anti-hybrid elections under Law 23 of 2020 implementing BEPS Action 2 and Action 3. No fiscal transparency election is allowed for a commercial S.A.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic turnover threshold triggers ITBMS registration; every person or legal entity that carries out taxable transfers of goods or services in Panama, or imports goods, must register with ANIP and obtain an RUC from the first taxable transaction. A reduced compliance regime ('Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente') is available for annual gross income not exceeding B/.150,000 (Balboas), but registration remains mandatory once taxable activity begins.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing (Factura Electrónica – FE) for registered taxpayers on a phased schedule. Invoices must be transmitted in real time to ANIP through the authorized electronic invoicing platform or via ANIP-approved API/Web Services, and each invoice must receive a tax-authority validation code and a QR code. No invoice may be legally issued without the ANIP digital authentication; non-validated invoices are not deductible or creditable. The system contemplates four control modes: online transmission, offline contingency, mobile/portable facturador, and ERP integration.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods are zero-rated (0% ITBMS) when the goods are physically removed from Panama under a valid customs export declaration and the exporter retains evidence of title transfer to a foreign buyer. Services, including franchise royalties and software or supply-chain management services, are outside the Panamanian ITBMS scope if the recipient is non-resident, the service is wholly performed outside Panama, or the benefit is enjoyed abroad. The supplier must be registered, file export statements, and maintain contemporaneous documentation proving the economic activity took place outside Panama. Input ITBMS directly attributable to zero-rated or non-taxed exports is creditable, and excess credits may be offset against other taxes or refunded following ANIP verification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera – DUA)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Currency Wire Receipt from a Panamanian bank demonstrating receipt of export proceeds
Export contract, purchase order, and proof of foreign buyer identity
ITBMS Export Certificate or ANIP export-supporting declaration (when required)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or inadequately documented export zero-rating claims are subject to immediate rejection, retrospective clawback of any refunded ITBMS, monetary indexation, and interest accruing from the date of the original refund. Administrative penalties may reach up to 200% of the tax understated or refunded, and criminal tax fraud convictions carry imprisonment of 2 to 5 years under Panamanian law. Failure to repatriate foreign sales proceeds within 180 days may cause the foreign revenue to be recharacterized as taxable Panama-source income and invalidate the zero-rating substantiation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) as the primary banking regulator, with Banco Nacional de Panamá as the state-owned financial agent but not a central bank capable of issuing domestic currency; fiscal and monetary policy coordination through the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized economy using the United States Dollar (USD) as legal tender; both current account and capital account transactions are freely convertible with no restrictions on inbound or outbound transfers; profit remittances require no special governmental approval beyond standard bank compliance documentation; the absence of a central bank means no domestic exchange controls exist, and repatriation of dividends, royalties, and franchise fees is unrestricted when supported by proper corporate and tax documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratios apply to export proceeds in Panama; exporters may freely retain, disburse, or repatriate all foreign-currency receipts without any obligation to convert into local currency; the only administrative requirement is accurate reporting to the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) for territorial tax compliance and compliance with anti-money laundering (AML) transaction reporting thresholds under the Superintendencia de Bancos.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banco Nacional de Panamá (State-owned, full commercial banking license)
Banco General (Largest private commercial bank in Panama)
Multibank (Multinational commercial bank with regional reach)
BAC Credomatic Panamá (Consumer and commercial banking arm of BAC International)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate feasibility; Panama does not have a dedicated e-money institution (EMI) licensing framework comparable to the EU, but fintechs may operate under the general non-bank financial services regime through the SBP's fintech law (Article 3 of the Decree Law 2 of 2018); unlicensed offshore digital EMIs cannot directly hold client funds or provide payment services in Panama without partnering with a licensed local bank; however, digital EMIs can process cross-border payments using correspondent banking and open virtual accounts through Panama's SWIFT-connected banking system; the viability rating for using an offshore EMI as a primary treasury vehicle is 'Low' due to strict AML correspondent banking due-diligence and the risk of de-risking by international partners, while an EMI with a local SBP license or a bank-backed fintech arrangement is rated 'Medium'.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the legal representative (redacted, typically the president or treasurer) and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is generally mandatory at the initial account-opening interview with the bank's compliance officer, especially for corporate structures using bearer share or PIF vehicles; remote opening is permitted for renewals and routine updates, but first-time onboarding requires at least one director or appointed agent to appear physically or through a Panamanian notarized power-of-attorney to a local legal counsel; banks may accept video conference KYC interviews only for signatory updates, not for primary account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Franchise corporate structure with foreign UBO and a Sociedad Anónima registered in Panama but lacking local economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate registry certification (Copia Simple), certificate of good standing, registered agent confirmation, UBO declaration form, audited financial statements or business plan, evidence of local office lease or franchise licensing activity in Panama, tax ID (RUC) certificate, and DGI income tax filing showing territorial-source royalties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border royalty inflows from multiple countries subject to differing withholding tax and double-tax agreements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed franchise agreements, royalty calculation formulas, evidence of commercial registration of trademark in Panama, invoices from the Panamanian entity to foreign franchisees, transfer pricing documentation demonstrating arm's length royalties, and bank statements of inbound wires with clear remitter and payment purpose codes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions involving countries or merchants flagged for sanctions or high AML risk in the bubble tea supply chain (e.g., certain Asian processing plants)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rigorous counterparty due diligence file, copies of customs declarations (SUNAT/ customs forms), shipping bills of lading, and supply-chain documentation; clear contractual warranties that the syrup supplier is not a sanctioned entity; a negative news screening report and OFAC/SDG watch-list checks for all counterparties above the threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large cash-deposit patterns from local POS and retail franchise outlets in Panama
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant acquiring agreement with the credit-card processor, sales reconciliation reports, point-of-sale (POS) settlement statements, inventory turnover reports, and tax filings (ISR declarations) demonstrating consistency between reported revenue and bank deposits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of intermediary corporate layers or a private interest foundation (PIF) to hold the franchise IP
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PIF foundation charter, beneficiary declarations, legal opinion on the non-disclosure of beneficiary under Panamanian law, background information on the foundation's agent, and evidence of the foundation's valid registration with the Registro Público, plus sworn declarations from the UBO clarifying the purpose of the structure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant capital inflows from foreign franchise investors should be routed via SWIFT MT103 messages to a Panamanian commercial bank using standardized purpose codes, commonly 'FDI' (foreign direct investment) or 'Genesis' codes under PAN liquidity reporting, with supporting capital contribution agreements, share purchase documents, and bank confirmation of the exact business purpose; all inbound funds must be sourced from the identified investor's bank account and be free of any connection to high-risk jurisdictions; for a Panama S.A., capital injections can be reflected as paid-in capital or subordinated shareholders' loans; the bank requires the completion of the 'Oringo' (Foreign Exchange and Capital Transactions) form only if the transaction exceeds US$10,000 for AML reporting, or if the bank's internal controls set a lower threshold; the routing must avoid cash or precious-metals couriers and use direct correspondent banks of the Panama bank (typically in the US or Europe) to maintain regulatory continuity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for syrup, packaging, and equipment purchases must be executed through SWIFT MT103 wires from the Panamanian operational account, accompanied by commercial invoices, packing lists, and customs declarations; for higher-value or highly regular supply purchases, a commercial documentary letter of credit (LC, UCP 600) may be established at a Panamanian bank, with the beneficiary bank and the shipping documentation (bill of lading, commercial invoice, certificate of origin) specified in the LC terms; all disbursements above the bank's due-diligence threshold require transaction-level screening against OFAC sanction lists and FATF watchlists; recommended rails are the SWIFT gpi network for rapid and traceable payments, and the local ACH (ACH Panama) for settlements to domestic suppliers and franchise employees.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: No local FX forward products are typically needed owing to full dollarization, but Panamanian banks and international broker-dealers may offer cross-currency swaps and FX forwards for non-USD foreign exchange risk (e.g., exposure to CNY or EUR in franchise royalty or syrup purchases); such derivatives are permissible under SBP license rules and are executed through a bank-approved master agreement (ISDA) to be documented as part of treasury policy.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not prohibited but are rarely used in Panama because the USD is legal tender, making currency risk primarily secondary to trade-partner currencies; banks will permit NDFs on minor currencies if the underlying commercial transaction is proven.

Currency swaps (cross-currency interest-rate swaps) may be arranged with foreign counterparty banks for multi-year franchise revenue hedging, subject to credit-risk limits and intra-committee approval; Panamanian banks do not require special regulatory authorization for hedging derivatives, but transaction reporting to the SBP under the derivatives statistics mandate applies for notional amounts exceeding USD 1 million.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Pago de Impuesto de Franquicia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before June 30 each calendar year; no instalment regime for S.A. entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a B/.50 surcharge plus monthly legal interest at approximately 1.5%. Unpaid franchise tax for three consecutive years exposes the S.A. to administrative strike-off in the Public Registry and cancellation of the legal entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta – Form 101)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year S.A., due on or before April 30 annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is penalised with tiered fines from B/.100 to B/.5,000, monthly interest on any omitted payable tax, and possible suspension of the taxpayer's RUC registration until the return is regularised.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registered Agent and UBO Confirmation (Confirmación de Beneficiarios Finales y Accionistas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público) through the licensed Resident Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before June 30, aligned with the franchise-tax payment cycle, and within 15 business days after any shareholding transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-confirmation prevents issuance of Good Standing certificates, blocks Registry endorsements, and exposes the Resident Agent to AML penalties under Law 2/2011 and Law 254/2021. The entity may be barred from registry procedures until the confirmation is completed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified audit by a Panamanian licensed CPA is mandatory if gross annual income exceeds USD 500,000 or total assets exceed USD 1,000,000; the DGI may also require audited statements under formal tax-risk criteria.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama; smaller non-listed entities may apply IFRS for SMEs if annual revenue is below USD 500,000 and they have no public accountability.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Resident Agent completes an annual KYC and beneficial-ownership confirmation for each S.A., verifying each shareholder's name, nationality, residence and percentage interest. Any share transfer must be notarised, recorded in the Register of Members within 30 days, and reported to the DGI under the IUSII share-transfer tax rules where applicable. A no-change annual confirmation is still required to maintain good standing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (Acta de Junta Directiva y de Accionistas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600–1,200 per year for accredited resident agent, registered office, and UBO-file custody; USD 1,500 if enhanced due-diligence or translation services are added.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000–8,000 per year for a low-risk franchise and intellectual-property holding vehicle, depending on transaction volume and local-source income reporting.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial scope: exemption for foreign-source franchise royalties and foreign trade profits; Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime under Law 41 of 2007 grants 0% ISLR and 0% dividend WHT on qualified foreign-source income for 25 years; micro/small taxpayer progressive regime (0%-15%) applies where annual gross income is below B/.200,000; dividend WHT reduced from 10% to 5% where the entity's effective CIT burden reaches at least 4% of taxable income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 820 (ISLR-Sociedades) annual corporate income tax return; filed online through the DGI E-Tax 2.0 electronic portal after digital authentication of the legal representative or appointed accountant.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within three months following the fiscal year-end, i.e., 15 March for calendar-year entities; the tax liability may be settled in up to three instalments with the first instalment due on the filing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1 - Ingresos brutos de fuente panameña
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Panama-source income: franchise royalties paid by Panamanian franchisees, Panama-local syrup and concentrate sales, on-premise boba-tea receipts, and management fees for services rendered in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owned S.A.: include all revenue arising from IP exploitation contracts with Panamanian franchisees even where the franchisee wires funds from overseas bank accounts; transfer-pricing adjustments apply to royalty rates charged to related local franchisees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source revenues excluded from the taxable base under territoriality, including royalties from master franchisees operating outside Panama and export sales where title and risk pass abroad.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose exclusively in the informational annex and preserve evidence of foreign situs: foreign IP registrations, sub-license agreements, and bills of lading; misclassifying Panama-source income as foreign-source is a criminal fraud red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses and cost of goods sold directly allocable to Panama-source revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Global head-office cost allocations and cross-border intercompany royalties must be supported by a contemporaneous transfer-pricing Local File; expenses attributable to exempt foreign-source income are non-deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating loss carryforward applied against current-year Panama-source taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Utilisation limited to five fiscal years; losses must derive exclusively from Panama-source activities and cannot offset foreign-source profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deductions and loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% statutory rate; the CAIR 2% gross-receipts minimum tax floor has been suspended by successive fiscal laws and must be revalidated for the specific filing year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance income tax payments, third-party withholdings, and treaty withholding credits applied against the final liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile prepared advance payment vouchers and any Panama WHT suffered; excess credits are recoverable through the formal DGI refund procedure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 7 - Impuesto a pagar o saldo a favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final annual tax payable or overpayment carried as a credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Settle through authorised bank channels; any unpaid balance accrues a 1.5% monthly surcharge plus consumer-price-index adjustment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a progressive fine of 10%-20% of the assessed tax plus a monthly 1.5% late-payment interest charge and CPI revaluation; non-fling authorises a DGI estimate based on prior three-year average gross receipts; evasion above B/.50,000 constitutes criminal tax fraud under Law 8 of 2019 with imprisonment of 3-5 years.
